title: Rabbi Chuna son of Rabbi Yose
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Taanit, chapter 4, end of halakhah 5: “Rabbi Chunah bar Yosef said: They went into exile by way of the deep.” The statement is cited in Eichah Rabbah at the end of the Petichtot, and there “Rabbi Chuna in the name of Rabbi Yose.” In Midrash Shmuel 20:11, Rabbi Huna bar Yosef; but the statement derives from Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 2:5, and there “Rabbi Huna in the name of Rabbi Yose.”

In Tanchuma, Noach 13: “Rabbi Huna son of Rabbi Yose says: Even a change of name annuls a harsh decree.” The statement in Bereshit Rabbah 44:12 is “Rabbi Huna bar Rav Yosef.” Hyman suggests that he is the third Rabbi Chuna, who was Rav Yosef’s student in Babylonia and afterward went up to the Land of Israel, as explained in his entry.

notes.text: The Taanit and Sanhedrin chapter/halakhah locations are Jerusalem Talmud. Hyman’s proposed father-versus-teacher reconstruction, third-Chuna identity and migration remain conjectural; Huna/Chuna and Yose/Yosef are not globally harmonized.

The consulted Bereshit Rabbah 44:12 directly names Rabbi Huna bar Rav Yosef. Father-versus-teacher readings, Huna/Chuna and Yose/Yosef forms, the third-Chuna identification and migration remain Hyman’s reconstruction.
